description: Found in defk-9p6.14. examples/pcm_mix.exs generates its s16le and s32le kernels from one quoted source (a defmacro returning `quote location: :keep do defk ... end end`, called as `PCM.Gen.mixer(:mix_s16, :flush_s16, i16, -32_768, 32_767)`). The kernels compile and run, but Defk.Report.print/1 lists all ~15 notes (bounds checks kept, vectorised or not, alloc zeroing) against the single call line, in one column, so you cannot tell which loop or access a note is about. `location: :keep` does not change it: the notes carry the caller line, not the :keep file/line. Workaround while tuning: write one kernel by hand (or in a scratch module), read its report, then generate. Options: use the :keep line/file from the quoted AST meta when present and print the macro module source; or print the note with the kernel-relative expression text (`bufs[base + i]: ...` is already there) grouped per loop. Done when: a kernel defined through a `location: :keep` macro gets its notes on the macro source lines (test in report_test).

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Notes for a kernel generated by a `quote location: :keep` macro point at the macro's source lines, not all at the call line

**Current behavior:**
A kernel defined through a macro that returns `quote location: :keep do defk ... end end` (examples/pcm_mix.exs, `PCM.Gen.mixer/5`) compiles and runs, but every fast-path report note (bounds checks, vectorised or not, alloc zeroing, ...) carries the single macro call line, so `Defk.Report.print/1` cannot say which loop or access a note is about.

**Desired behavior:**
- When the kernel's AST carries `:keep` location metadata (file and line from the macro source), each note uses that line, and the report shows the macro source file for those notes (a kernel defined in the module's own file prints as today).
- Without `location: :keep` the behaviour is unchanged (call line), and that is documented as how to get per-line notes.
- Compile errors in such kernels already follow whatever Elixir's location is; do not change them unless the same fix applies trivially (say in the report if so).

**Key interfaces:**
- `__defk_report__/0` facts `{kernel, line, fact}`: if a file is needed, extend the shape in a backwards-compatible way and document it in Defk.Report's types (unstable per ADR-0006)
- `Defk.Report.print/1` / `format/1` output; docs/fast-path-report.md

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] report_test: a kernel generated through a `location: :keep` macro (macro in a separate module/file under test/support) has notes on distinct lines matching the macro source
- [ ] The same macro without `:keep` keeps all notes on the call line
- [ ] examples/pcm_mix.exs's report shows per-line notes; drop its workaround note if it has one
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Grouping notes per loop, or new report topics
PR #7: https://github.com/DanielLuning/defk/pull/7 (sweep with defk-vcx.1, defk-9qv, defk-sbp, defk-nii, defk-xyz).

title: Defk.Report puts every note of a macro-generated kernel on the macro call line
